display.purpose: Hero name and the closing headline. Archivo 800 at wdth 118; 3.1rem phone, 5.2rem small, 3.6/4.75rem in the hero plate, up to 6rem at the close.

headline.purpose: Section h2s: 2.5rem / 3.75rem / 4.5rem by breakpoint, about 14ch wide.

title.purpose: Company, project and stage names: 1.9rem to 2.4rem; 1.7rem in the stage card.

body.purpose: Reading copy in bone-dim at 1rem to 1.125rem, line-height 1.625, capped near 38rem or 65ch.

label.purpose: Dates, level numbers, status, tool tags, skill group names. Uppercase, 0.08em tracking, tabular figures.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for hover, link underline, entrances and stage swaps.

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.purpose: Buttons and level keys lift on hover.

motion.name: hero-rise
motion.purpose: Hero copy entrance, once on load; the stage column follows from 380ms.

motion.name: stage-swap
motion.purpose: Stage card content changes, arriving from the path direction.

motion.name: scroll-spring
motion.value: spring stiffness 170, damping 32, mass 0.5 on scroll progress
motion.purpose: Light inertia on every scroll-scrubbed value.

motion.name: scroll-arrive
motion.value: perspective(1200px) translate3d(slide, rise 48px, -depth 160px) rotateX(tilt) rotateY(swing) to rest; opacity 0.12 to 1
motion.purpose: Section content arriving from depth between 'start 100%' and 'start 58%'. Reversible; at rest before mount and under reduced motion.

motion.name: scroll-words
motion.purpose: The lead recommendation lights up as it is read.

motion.name: camera-spring
motion.value: spring k 26, c 9 with slight overshoot
motion.purpose: 3D camera flying to the selected island.

narrative.overview:
The career is a console world map at dusk. Every role is a floating, toon-shaded diorama island on one dotted ochre path from 2018 to now, and choosing a level springs the camera to that island. The rest of the page reads like the pause menu of that game: square plates, condensed HUD labels, stretched stage titles, and four flat inks on a dark sky. Nothing is glossy; depth comes from the 3D world and from scroll-linked perspective, never from shadows or blur haze.

Density is low and editorial: one idea per section, one content edge, long dark fields between sections. The world is the only place colour gets loud; HTML surfaces stay bone on sky with ochre reserved for the path, selection and the single primary action.

Motion belongs to the camera. As you scroll, content arrives from depth along a perspective, scrubbed to scroll position and reversible, as if the camera were travelling over the map. Everything renders at rest before mount and under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Dusk sky ground with four flat inks (bone, moss, ochre, clay).
One family, Archivo, used across its width axis: stretched for titles, normal for reading, condensed for HUD.
Square corners everywhere; 1px bone hairlines; an ochre corner notch marks a stage plate.
Toon-shaded low-poly 3D: a signature overworld hero and one smaller flag island at the close.
Scroll-scrubbed perspective motion on every section, transform and opacity only.

rules.name: The Four Inks Rule
rules.body: Every surface, HTML or 3D, is drawn in sky plus bone, moss, ochre and clay. A new hue needs a world reason, not a section reason.

rules.name: The Ochre Means Here Rule
rules.body: Ochre marks position, selection or the one primary action in view. Never use it for decoration or for a second competing button.

rules.name: The Clay Stays In The World Rule
rules.body: Clay lives on the islands. HTML text and controls do not use it.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo is the only face. Contrast comes from the width axis and weight, never from a second family.

rules.name: The Width Means Role Rule
rules.body: Stretched is a name (a stage, a section, a company). Condensed is data (a date, a number, a status). Normal width is for reading.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separation is a hairline or a tonal step, never a drop shadow. Plates float because the world behind them moves, not because they cast anything.

rules.name: The Toon Not Gloss Rule
rules.body: 3D materials are toon-shaded with a three-step ramp or flat unlit ochre. No PBR gloss, no bloom, no glow haze.

dos: Do keep every surface in sky plus the four inks; check new text against the 4.5:1 floor (bone-mute is the dimmest text colour allowed).
Do use the width axis for role: stretched 800 for names and headings, condensed 600 uppercase tracked for dates, numbers and status.
Do keep corners square and frames to 1px bone hairlines; mark a featured panel with the ochre corner notch.
Do scrub scroll motion to position with transform and opacity, let it reverse on scroll-up, and render at rest before mount and under reduced motion.
Do give 3D a still fallback (reduced motion, low memory) and an HTML-only fallback (no WebGL, save-data), and pause rendering when it is off screen.
Do keep every fact that appears in 3D also present in HTML.
donts: Don't add box shadows, glows, glassmorphism or backdrop blur to HTML surfaces.
Don't round corners on buttons, plates, images or tags.
Don't introduce a second typeface or a new accent hue.
Don't use clay for text or controls, or ochre for decoration.
Don't add gloss, bloom or PBR materials to the world; keep the three-step toon ramp.
Don't add a third real-time 3D scene; the overworld and the flag island are the budget.
